summary: Implemented the rddev Go CLI and the task state machine. Command skeleton per specs/orchestrator/rddev-cli.yaml: doctor (full ops/doctor-checks.md port, exit 0/1/2/3), env up|down (real docker compose wrappers), env reset|gc (honest stubs, exit 4), task next|ready|inspect|verify|accept|reject|merged, worker */git commit/pr open|merge (honest stubs naming T0010/T0011/T0012, exit 4 — never silent no-ops). Task state machine in internal/devorchestrator: 9 states, legal-transition enforcement (illegal transitions rejected, state file unchanged), dependency satisfaction = all deps merged, atomic writes (temp+fsync+rename) serialized by flock, run_id + UTC timestamp on every change, append-only history, unknown-field preservation (non-clobbering). rddev doctor is byte-identical to ops/doctor.sh for identical inputs (verified both via the 16-case fixture port and in real mode on this host). Human output by default, --json for machines, both tested. Stdlib only; go.mod/go.sum untouched.

tests.command: rddev doctor --json vs ./ops/doctor.sh --json (real mode, this host, no fixture)
tests.evidence: both exit 0; `cmp /tmp/doctor-go.json /tmp/doctor-bash.json` → BYTE-IDENTICAL. Human mode: `diff` shows exactly one difference, line 1 (script name 'rddev doctor' vs 'ops/doctor.sh'). The parity is also enforced in-repo by TestParityWithBashReference against the canonical fixture in both modes.

acceptance.criterion: rddev task next 只返回 dependencies 满足的任务
acceptance.evidence: Store.Next() filters status ∈ {todo, ready} AND all dependencies merged (docs/30 §3). TestNextOnlyDependencySatisfied: with T1000 merged, next returns exactly [T1001, T1003] and excludes T1002 (depends on unmerged T1001). Real-repo smoke test: `rddev task next --json` returns [] because T0009's dependency T0004 is still running — the exclusion is correct, and the empty pool emits [] not null.

Transition table enforced in internal/devorchestrator/state.go (recorded in specs/orchestrator/task-state-machine.yaml). TestEveryIllegalTransitionRejectedAndFileUnchanged drives every illegal from→to pair and byte-compares the state file before/after: rejected, never coerced. CLI-level: TestCLIIllegalTransitionLeavesFileUnchanged (accept from accepted → exit 1, file byte-unchanged) and the subprocess race loser exits 1 with 'illegal state transition'.

acceptance.criterion: 并发写状态不会静默覆盖
acceptance.evidence: All mutations serialize on an exclusive flock (per-open-file-description, so it conflicts across goroutines and processes) and commit via temp file + fsync + rename. TestConcurrentWritersDoNotSilentlyOverwrite: 8 goroutines race `accept` — exactly 1 succeeds, 7 fail loudly with IllegalTransitionError, history has exactly the committed entries. TestSubprocessConcurrencyRunsTwoRealProcesses exercises the same guarantee across two real OS processes: exactly one exit 0, one exit 1, history length 1, no leftover temp files.

Every command has help (exit 0, usage on stdout) and deterministic JSON output (compact, SetEscapeHTML(false), trailing newline, fixed field order). Tested: main_test.go (help content, version, unknown subcommand exit 2, doctor delegation exit 0/3), task_test.go (next/ready/inspect/transition JSON shapes, empty pools as [], subprocess JSON field-by-field), env_test.go (stub JSON error object {error, exit_code}), doctor_test.go (TestJSONShapeContract: 35 checks in contract order, summary counts consistent).

risks: L1: the transition table was not previously written down; recorded in specs/orchestrator/task-state-machine.yaml (todo→[ready,blocked], ready→[running,blocked], running→[verification,worker_failed,rejected], verification→[accepted,rejected], worker_failed/rejected/blocked→[ready], accepted→[merged], merged→terminal). Supervisor confirmation requested in G2.
L1: `task merged` (accepted→merged, stamps merged_at) is implemented as Supervisor merge bookkeeping so the state machine is complete before T0012; T0012 may fold it into pr merge.
L1: bare `rddev task ready` lists the ready pool; `task ready TASK` performs the transition (docs/61 shows the bare form without an argument).

L1: rddev uses the current directory as the repo root (documented 'run from the repo root'); --tasks-json/--state-json override. The default state lock is .rddev/locks/task_status.lock (untracked runtime dir per rddev-cli.yaml); overridden state paths get a sibling .lock.
L1: general CLI usage errors exit 2 while doctor usage errors exit 3 (contract ops/doctor-checks.md §2). Consistent with the T0002 scaffold's exit 2 for unknown subcommands.

env up/down are real `docker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 300` / `docker compose down` wrappers (docs/66) but were NOT exercised against a real daemon in this task — the Worker environment has no Docker socket grant (worker-guard). The compose command construction is unit-tested via an injected runner seam; live verification is deferred to G3.

env reset/gc are honest stubs (exit 4) pending the infra clients of T0010/T0011; the reset/gc flag surface (--test-only/--all-dev-data/--confirm) is parsed and validated but the destructive operations belong to the namespace-management subsystem (docs/66 §4 forbids Workers from running uncontrolled prunes).

worker spawn|list|logs|stop, git commit, pr open|merge are honest stubs exiting 4 with the owning task named (T0010/T0011/T0012) — never silent no-ops. Stub messages are emitted on stderr in human mode and as a JSON error object {error, exit_code} on stdout in --json mode (choice: machine consumers read stdout JSON, humans read stderr).
run_id defaults to a freshly generated crypto/rand id and is reported in the output; --run-id accepts a Supervisor-supplied id.
The reject command requires --reason or --reason-file (docs/61 shows --reason-file); the reason is recorded in rejection_reason and in the history entry.
notes_for_supervisor: 1) The worker-guard hook blocks Bash command text containing git-control-plane or Docker keywords on this Worker box, so the live smoke test of `rddev git commit`/`rddev pr ...` (which are exit-4 stubs performing zero git operations) could not be run from the shell — their behavior is covered by unit tests instead. 2) T0009's DAG dependency T0004 is still running, so `rddev task next` legitimately returns [] for the real repo right now; once T0004 merges, T0009 becomes dispatchable by the machine (deps T0002 merged + T0004 running). 3) rddev doctor is byte-identical to ops/doctor.sh in real mode on this host (both JSON and human output, human differing only in the line-1 script name) — the ops/doctor.sh parity test in the doctor package enforces this in CI too. 4) No follow_up_issues were implemented (per the Worker contract); all forward-looking hooks are described in risks. 5) go.mod/go.sum were not touched (stdlib only), as required while the DB-dependency Worker owns them.
